title: 顶点删除与整体同伦型
scope: Only MG-P001 in the staging suite. No public-suite integration, runner edit, model calibration, commit, or push.

primary_locations: Biss 2003 Annals 158, printed pp.947-949, especially Proposition 4.5 proof on p.948; Proposition 2.6 context on p.936.
Mnev arXiv:0709.1291v3, 18 September 2007, both pages, especially p.1.
Biss 2009 Annals 170, printed p.493, author erratum.
provenance.historical_status: The author acknowledged a gluing proof error; Theorem 1.1 remained a conjecture in the 2009 erratum. This is not a disproof of that theorem and is not a claim about the full 2026 research status.

retained: A contractible open subset O and a closed subset C cover X.
The actual inclusion O intersection C into C is a homotopy equivalence.
The topology is the geometric-realization topology of finite combinatorial objects.
changed: Replace the original oriented-matroid posets with arbitrary finite abstract simplicial complexes.
Restrict the deleted subcomplex to one distinguished vertex v.
Replace the failed universal-contractibility inference with a true possible-homotopy-type classification, complete realization family, and exact local contractibility test.
not_claimed: This task is not Proposition 4.5 or Theorem 1.1 of the original paper.
A noncontractible adapted example does not refute the original matroid theorem.
The source does not supply the new suspension classification or the full criterion.
No claim of empirical difficulty follows from the historical proof failure.

terminal_result.model: |K| is homotopy equivalent to the unreduced suspension of |link_K(v)|; the link has at least one vertex.
terminal_result.range: Exactly the homotopy types of suspensions of finite simplicial complexes with at least one vertex; realizations use two cones and one edge B.
terminal_result.criterion: All reduced integral homology groups of link_K(v) vanish, equivalently its finite augmented integral chain complex is exact.
terminal_result.not_a_cancellation_theorem: The description is a possible-type range, not a claim that suspension reflects homotopy equivalence.

proof_dependency_chain: The inclusion of punctured B cannot surject on path components if v is isolated, hence the link is nonempty.
Normalize barycentric coordinates away from v to obtain a strong deformation retraction of O onto K-v.
The deletion subcomplex is contractible and forms a CW pair with K.
Collapse the contractible closed deletion subcomplex and identify the quotient with cone(link)/link, hence the suspension.
Every finite nonempty link occurs in the two-cone construction; a single closed edge gives the required B condition.
Suspension Mayer-Vietoris yields necessity of integral acyclicity, including reduced H0.
Acyclic link is path connected; van Kampen gives a simply connected suspension, then Hurewicz and Whitehead give contractibility.
The local face data determines finite integer boundary matrices, so Smith normal form tests the criterion.

shortest_legal_route.description: An expert may state the punctured-vertex deformation retraction, invoke the valid CW quotient theorem to identify the suspension, realize arbitrary links by a simplicial suspension and an edge, and apply the standard suspension-acyclicity criterion with its simple-connectivity justification.
shortest_legal_route.single_counterexample_status: A circle refutes only an unrequested stronger assertion; it does not establish the requested range, all realizations and exact local test.

temptation.historical_shortcut: Replace C by O intersection C in the open/closed union solely because their inclusion is a homotopy equivalence, and infer X is homotopy equivalent to O.
temptation.correct_distinction: The proof instead uses the actual closed deletion subcomplex and its CW-pair quotient. The complete family can have any finite suspension type.
temptation.secondary_overrestriction: Demand a contractible link although a merely integral-acyclic link suffices.

optional_author_controls: One-vertex link produces a contractible interval.
Two isolated link vertices produce a circle while satisfying exactly the same cover hypotheses.
Finite sphere links realize every positive-dimensional sphere.

A balanced two-relator finite presentation complex has integral boundary determinant 1 and a nontrivial permutation image of its fundamental group; a finite simplicial model is an acyclic noncontractible link whose suspension is contractible.

formalization.reason: No actual-object Lean proof of the geometric realization, suspension, and homotopy/homology argument is supplied. A finite matrix lemma would not constitute coverage of the task.

unresolved_issues: No candidate model trial or demonstrated discrimination.
